message.content: {"label": "ASK", "response": "The S5 rules describe two urea schedules for garlic in southern Tigray at 150 kg urea/ha: a two-application schedule (half at planting, half 30-45 days after planting) and an optional three-application schedule (1/3 at planting, 1/3 at 30 days, final 1/3 three weeks later) that applies only 'when there is good rain.' Because the three-split option is conditional on rainfall, I cannot choose between two and three splits for your farm without knowing your rainfall/water situation this season. Please tell me whether rainfall/soil moisture this season is expected to be good.", "justification": "The two-split urea schedule (r_c10_urea_2split) is the described regional practice at 150 kg urea/ha, and the three-split schedule (r_c10_urea_3split) is a MAY option conditioned on 'good rain' (rainfall = good), a threshold not numerically defined. The farmer's rainfall is UNKNOWN, so the applicable rule cannot be resolved. The general N rule (r_c11_n_rate) gives a nutrient range and a 2-3 later-split schedule but no field-specific selection, and the bulbing advisory (r_c11_no_n_bulbing) depends on an unknown growth stage. A specific farmer fact (rainfall/water availability) would change which schedule applies, so ASK is appropriate.", "rule_ids": ["r_c10_urea_2split", "r_c10_urea_3split", "r_c11_n_rate", "r_c11_no_n_bulbing"], "cited_pages": [12], "missing_facts": ["rainfall", "growth_stage"]}
